note: Latin–English renderings corrected against the Clementine Latin, 2 November 2026. Each entry: card, reference, old and new English, and the reason. An independent second reading checked every correction; nine it judged unnecessary were reverted before publishing.

corrections.old: Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt: and he was there until the death of Herod:
corrections.new: Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt:
corrections.reason: English added 'and he was there until the death of Herod', which belongs to Latin verse 15 ('et erat ibi usque ad obitum Herodis'), not this verse.

corrections.old: That it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son.
corrections.new: And he was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son.
corrections.reason: English omitted 'et erat ibi usque ad obitum Herodis' (and he was there until the death of Herod), which opens this Latin verse.

corrections.old: For he was teaching them as one having power, and not as the scribes and Pharisees.
corrections.new: For he was teaching them as one having power, and not as their scribes and Pharisees.
corrections.reason: English omitted 'eorum' (their) in 'sicut scribae eorum, et pharisaei'.

corrections.old: And they came to him, and awaked him, saying: Lord, save us, we perish.
corrections.new: And his disciples came to him, and awaked him, saying: Lord, save us, we perish.
corrections.reason: English omitted the subject 'discipuli ejus' (his disciples) in 'accesserunt ad eum discipuli ejus'.

corrections.old: And when Jesus had come into the house of the ruler, and saw the minstrels and the multitude making a rout,
corrections.new: And when Jesus had come into the house of the ruler, and saw the minstrels and the multitude making a rout, he said:
corrections.reason: Latin verse ends with "dicebat:" (he said), which the English omitted here and placed in the next verse.

corrections.old: He said: Give place, for the girl is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.
corrections.new: Give place, for the girl is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn.
corrections.reason: Latin verse has no verb of speaking ("dicebat" ends the previous verse); removed the added "He said:".

corrections.old: These twelve Jesus sent: commanding them, saying: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into the city of the Samaritans enter you not.
corrections.new: These twelve Jesus sent: commanding them, saying: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into the cities of the Samaritans enter you not.
corrections.reason: Latin "in civitates" is plural: cities, not city.

corrections.old: And when they shall persecute you in this city, flee into another. Amen, I say to you, you shall not finish all the cities of Israel, until the Son of Man come.
corrections.new: And when they shall persecute you in this city, flee into another. Amen, I say to you, you shall not finish the cities of Israel, until the Son of Man come.
corrections.reason: Latin "non consummabitis civitates Israel" has no word for "all"; removed the addition.

corrections.old: And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven allows violence, and the violent bear it away.
corrections.new: And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent bear it away.
corrections.reason: Latin "vim patitur" means suffers (undergoes) violence, not "allows violence."

corrections.old: And when he had passed from there, he came into their synagogues.
corrections.new: And when he had passed from there, he came into their synagogue.
corrections.reason: Latin "synagogam" is singular: synagogue, not synagogues.

corrections.old: And when he had come to the multitude, there came to him a man falling down on his knees before him saying: Lord, have pity on my son, for he is a afflicted by the moon, and allows much: for he falls often into the fire, and often into the water.
corrections.new: And when he had come to the multitude, there came to him a man falling down on his knees before him saying: Lord, have pity on my son, for he is afflicted by the moon, and suffers much: for he falls often into the fire, and often into the water.
corrections.reason: Latin 'male patitur' means 'suffers much', not 'allows much'; also removes a stray 'a' before 'afflicted'.

corrections.old: Jesus said to them: Because of your unbelief. For, amen I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain: Remove from here here, and it shall remove: and nothing shall be impossible to you.
corrections.new: Jesus said to them: Because of your unbelief. For, amen I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain: Remove from here to there, and it shall remove: and nothing shall be impossible to you.
corrections.reason: Latin 'Transi hinc illuc' means 'from here to there'; the English repeated 'here'.

corrections.old: Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
corrections.new: Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind on earth will be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed also in heaven.
corrections.reason: Latin 'erunt ligata et in cælo' and 'erunt soluta et in cælo' include 'et' (also), which the English omitted.

corrections.old: It shall not be so among you: but whoever is the greater among you, let him be your minister.
corrections.new: It shall not be so among you: but whoever wishes to become the greater among you, let him be your minister.
corrections.reason: Latin 'quicumque voluerit inter vos major fieri' means 'whoever wishes to become greater', not 'whoever is the greater'.

corrections.old: Saying to them: Go into the village that is over against you: and immediately you shall find an donkey tied and a colt with her. Loose them and bring them to me.
corrections.new: Saying to them: Go into the village that is over against you: and immediately you shall find a donkey tied and a colt with her. Loose them and bring them to me.
corrections.reason: Typography: "an donkey".

corrections.old: Tell you the daughter of Zion: Behold your king comes to you, meek and sitting upon an donkey and a colt, the foal of her that is used to the yoke.
corrections.new: Tell you the daughter of Zion: Behold your king comes to you, meek and sitting upon a donkey and a colt, the foal of her that is used to the yoke.
corrections.reason: Typography: "an donkey".

corrections.old: And the foolish said to the wise: Give us of your oil, for our lamps have gone out.
corrections.new: And the foolish said to the wise: Give us of your oil, for our lamps are going out.
corrections.reason: Latin 'extinguuntur' is present (are going out), not completed 'have gone out'.

corrections.old: But Jesus said: Go into the city to a certain man and say to him: The master says, My time is near near. With you I make the pasch with my disciples.
corrections.new: But Jesus said: Go into the city to a certain man and say to him: The master says, My time is near. With you I make the pasch with my disciples.
corrections.reason: Duplicated 'near near'; Latin 'Tempus meum prope est' has a single 'prope'.

corrections.old: Then he comes to his disciples and said to them: Sleep you now and take your rest. Behold the hour is near: and the Son of Man shall be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
corrections.new: Then he comes to his disciples and says to them: Sleep you now and take your rest. Behold the hour is near: and the Son of Man shall be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
corrections.reason: Latin 'dicit illis' is present, matching 'venit'; 'said' changed to 'says'.

corrections.old: They therefore being gathered together, Pilate said: Whom will you that I release to You: Barabbas, or Jesus that is called Christ?
corrections.new: They therefore being gathered together, Pilate said: Whom will you that I release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus that is called Christ?
corrections.reason: Latin 'vobis' addresses the crowd; capital 'You' wrongly suggests Jesus is addressed. Changed to 'you'.

corrections.old: Pilate says to them: What shall I do then with Jesus that is called Christ? They say all: Let him be crucified.
corrections.new: Pilate says to them: What shall I do then with Jesus that is called Christ?
corrections.reason: 'They say all: Let him be crucified' renders 'Dicunt omnes: Crucifigatur', which belongs to Latin verse 23, not this verse.

corrections.old: The governor said to them: Why, what evil has he done? But they cried out the more, saying: Let him be crucified.
corrections.new: They say all: Let him be crucified. The governor said to them: Why, what evil has he done? But they cried out the more, saying: Let him be crucified.
corrections.reason: Latin begins 'Dicunt omnes: Crucifigatur', which the English omitted; restored as 'They say all: Let him be crucified.'

corrections.old: And he says to them: Are you ignorant of this, parable? and how shall you know all parables?
corrections.new: And he says to them: Are you ignorant of this parable? and how shall you know all parables?
corrections.reason: A stray comma in 'this, parable' breaks Latin 'parabolam hanc' (this parable) into a vocative; removed it.

corrections.old: And he was in the hinder part of the boat, sleeping upon a pillow; and they awake him, and say to him: Master, does, it not concern you that we perish?
corrections.new: And he was in the hinder part of the boat, sleeping upon a pillow; and they awake him, and say to him: Master, does it not concern you that we perish?
corrections.reason: A stray comma in 'does, it not' garbles Latin 'non ad te pertinet' (does it not concern you); removed it.

corrections.old: But sending an executioner, he commanded that his head should be brought in a dish.
corrections.new: But sending an executioner, he commanded that his head should be brought in a dish. And he beheaded him in the prison,
corrections.reason: English omitted Latin 'Et decollavit eum in carcere' (and he beheaded him in prison), which this Latin verse contains; restored it here.

corrections.old: And he beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head in a dish: and gave it to the damsel, and the damsel gave it to her mother.
corrections.new: And brought his head in a dish: and gave it to the damsel, and the damsel gave it to her mother.
corrections.reason: English opened with 'And he beheaded him in the prison', which belongs to Latin 6:27; this Latin verse begins 'et attulit caput ejus'.

corrections.old: And crying out and greatly tearing him, he went our of him. And he became as dead, so that many said: He is dead.
corrections.new: And crying out and greatly tearing him, he went out of him. And he became as dead, so that many said: He is dead.
corrections.reason: Typo: 'went our of him' must read 'went out of him' for Latin 'exiit ab eo'.

corrections.old: And they came to Jerusalem. And when he had entered into the temple, he began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple: and over threw the tables of the moneychangers and the chairs of them that sold doves.
corrections.new: And they came to Jerusalem. And when he had entered into the temple, he began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple: and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers and the chairs of them that sold doves.
corrections.reason: Typography: "over threw".

corrections.old: And that he should be loved with the whole heart and with the whole understanding and with the whole soul and with the whole strength. And to love one’s neighbour as one’s self is a greater thing than all holocausts and sacrifices.
corrections.new: And that he should be loved with the whole heart and with the whole understanding and with the whole soul and with the whole strength, and to love one’s neighbour as one’s self, is a greater thing than all holocausts and sacrifices.
corrections.reason: Full stop split the compound subject; Latin 'ut diligatur... et diligere proximum... majus est' makes both loves greater than holocausts.

corrections.old: And then if any man shall say to you: Lo, here is Christ. Lo, he is here: do not believe.
corrections.new: And then if any man shall say to you: Lo, here is Christ. Lo, he is there: do not believe.
corrections.reason: Latin 'ecce illic' means 'lo, there'; the English had 'Lo, he is here', repeating 'here'.

corrections.old: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my word shall not pass away.
corrections.new: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
corrections.reason: Latin 'verba... mea' is plural; the English had singular 'my word'.

corrections.old: He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children and the unbelieving to the understanding of the righteous, to prepare a people made ready for the Lord.
corrections.new: He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children and the unbelieving to the understanding of the righteous, to prepare a perfect people for the Lord.
corrections.reason: English "a people made ready" does not render Latin "plebem perfectam" (a perfect people).

corrections.old: And it happened, after the angels departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another: Let us go over to Bethlehem and let us see this word that has happen, which the Lord has showed to us.
corrections.new: And it happened, after the angels departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another: Let us go over to Bethlehem and let us see this word that has happened, which the Lord has showed to us.
corrections.reason: Ungrammatical 'has happen' corrected to 'has happened' for Latin 'quod factum est'.

corrections.old: And he brought him to Jerusalem and set him on a pinnacle of the temple and said to him: If you be the Son of God, cast yourself from here.
corrections.new: And he brought him to Jerusalem and set him on a pinnacle of the temple and said to him: If you be the Son of God, cast yourself down from here.
corrections.reason: Latin 'deorsum' (down) was missing; added 'down'.

corrections.old: But the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying to his disciples: Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?
corrections.new: But the Pharisees and their scribes murmured, saying to his disciples: Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?
corrections.reason: Latin 'scribae eorum' (their scribes): 'their' was missing; added.

corrections.old: Give: and it shall be given to you: good measure and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom. For with the same measure that you shall mete also, it shall be measured to you again.
corrections.new: Give: and it shall be given to you: good measure and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom. For with the same measure that you shall mete, it shall be measured to you again.
corrections.reason: 'Also' is not in the Latin 'qua mensi fueritis'; removed.

corrections.old: For he loves our nation: and he has built us a synagogue.
corrections.new: For he loves our nation: and he himself has built us a synagogue.
corrections.reason: Latin "ipse aedificavit" has the emphatic "ipse" (he himself), which the English omitted.

corrections.old: And the Pharisee, who had invited him, seeing it, spoke within himself, saying: This man, if he were if a prophet, would know surely who and what manner of woman this is that touches him, that she is a sinner.
corrections.new: And the Pharisee, who had invited him, seeing it, spoke within himself, saying: This man, if he were a prophet, would know surely who and what manner of woman this is that touches him, that she is a sinner.
corrections.reason: English duplicates "if" ("if he were if a prophet"); Latin "si esset propheta" has a single condition.

corrections.old: And it happened the day following, when they came down from the mountain, there met him a great multitude.
corrections.new: And it happened the day following, when they came down from the mountain, there met them a great multitude.
corrections.reason: Latin "occurrit illis" is plural (met them); the English had "met him".

corrections.old: And Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their dead: but go and preach the kingdom of God.
corrections.new: And Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their dead: but you go and preach the kingdom of God.
corrections.reason: Latin "tu autem vade" has the emphatic "tu" (but you go); the English dropped it.

corrections.old: He said: The one who showed mercy to him. And Jesus said to him: Go, and do likewise.
corrections.new: He said: The one who showed mercy to him. And Jesus said to him: Go, and you do likewise.
corrections.reason: Latin "Vade, et tu fac similiter" has the emphatic "tu" (and you do likewise); the English dropped it.

corrections.old: Now, if God clothe in this manner the grass that is to-day in the field and to-next day is cast into the oven: how much more you, O you of little faith?
corrections.new: Now, if God clothe in this manner the grass that is to-day in the field and to-morrow is cast into the oven: how much more you, O you of little faith?
corrections.reason: Latin "cras" (tomorrow); "to-next day" was a garbled modernisation.

corrections.old: And he said to them: Go and tell that fox: Behold, I cast out demons and do cures, to-day and to-next day, and the third day I am consummated.
corrections.new: And he said to them: Go and tell that fox: Behold, I cast out demons and do cures, to-day and to-morrow, and the third day I am consummated.
corrections.reason: Latin "cras" (tomorrow); "to-next day" was a garbled modernisation.

corrections.old: Nevertheless, I must walk to-day and to-next day and the day following, because it cannot be that a prophet perish, out of Jerusalem.
corrections.new: Nevertheless, I must walk to-day and to-morrow and the day following, because it cannot be that a prophet perish, out of Jerusalem.
corrections.reason: Latin "cras" (tomorrow); "to-next day" was a garbled modernisation.

corrections.old: And answering them, he said: Which of you shall have an donkey or an ox fall into a pit and will not immediately draw him out, on the sabbath day?
corrections.new: And answering them, he said: Which of you shall have a donkey or an ox fall into a pit and will not immediately draw him out, on the sabbath day?
corrections.reason: Typography: "an donkey".

corrections.old: I am not worthy to be called your son: make me as one of your hired servants.
corrections.new: I am no longer worthy to be called your son: make me as one of your hired servants.
corrections.reason: The English omitted Latin 'jam' (no longer), reading 'I am not worthy'; 'jam non sum dignus' means 'I am no longer worthy'.

corrections.old: And he said: Then, father, I implore you that you would send him to my father’s house, for I have five brothers,
corrections.new: And he said: Then, father, I implore you that you would send him to my father’s house.
corrections.reason: The English added 'for I have five brothers', which is not in this Latin verse; Latin 'habeo enim quinque fratres' opens verse 28.

corrections.old: That he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torments.
corrections.new: For I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torments.
corrections.reason: The English omitted Latin 'habeo enim quinque fratres' (for I have five brothers), which belongs to this verse.

corrections.old: Yet because this widow is troublesome to me, I will avenge her, lest continually coming she weary me.
corrections.new: Yet because this widow is troublesome to me, I will avenge her, lest coming at the last she weary me.
corrections.reason: Latin "in novissimo veniens" means coming at the last, not "continually coming."

corrections.old: Saying: Go into the town which is over against you, at your entering into which you shall find the colt of an donkey tied, on which no one ever has sitten: loose him and bring him here.
corrections.new: Saying: Go into the town which is over against you, at your entering into which you shall find the colt of a donkey tied, on which no one ever has sitten: loose him and bring him here.
corrections.reason: Typography: "an donkey".

corrections.old: And he was teaching daily in the temple. And the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people sought to destroy him.
corrections.new: And he was teaching daily in the temple. And the chief priests and the scribes and the ruler of the people sought to destroy him.
corrections.reason: Latin "princeps plebis" is singular, "the ruler of the people"; the English had the plural "rulers."

corrections.old: And when he rose up from prayer and had come to the disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow.
corrections.new: And when he rose up from prayer and had come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow.
corrections.reason: Latin 'ad discipulos suos' has the possessive 'his'; the English dropped it.

corrections.old: Whom when a certain servant maid had seen sitting at the light and had earnestly saw him, she said: This man also was with him.
corrections.new: Whom when a certain servant maid had seen sitting at the light and had earnestly beheld him, she said: This man also was with him.
corrections.reason: 'had earnestly saw him' is ungrammatical; Latin 'eum fuisset intuita' means had gazed at him (Douay 'beheld').

corrections.old: But the other answering, rebuked him, saying: Neither do you fear God, seeing; you are under the same condemnation?
corrections.new: But the other answering, rebuked him, saying: Neither do you fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?
corrections.reason: A stray semicolon after 'seeing' breaks the causal clause Latin 'quod in eadem damnatione es' (seeing you are under the same condemnation).

corrections.old: But Peter rising up, ran to the tomb and, stooping down, he saw the linen cloths laid by themselves: and went away wondering in himself at that which had happen.
corrections.new: But Peter rising up, ran to the tomb and, stooping down, he saw the linen cloths laid by themselves: and went away wondering in himself at that which had happened.
corrections.reason: Typo 'had happen' for 'had happened' (Latin 'quod factum fuerat').

corrections.old: And the one of them, whose name was Clopas, answered him: Are you only a stranger in Jerusalem, and have not known the things that have been done there in these days?
corrections.new: And the one of them, whose name was Cleophas, answered him: Are you only a stranger in Jerusalem, and have not known the things that have been done there in these days?
corrections.reason: Name wrong: Latin has 'Cleophas', not 'Clopas'.

corrections.old: And when he had made, as it were, a flog of little cords, he drove them all out of the temple, the sheep also and the oxen: and the money of the changers he poured out, and the tables he overthrew.
corrections.new: And when he had made, as it were, a scourge of little cords, he drove them all out of the temple, the sheep also and the oxen: and the money of the changers he poured out, and the tables he overthrew.
corrections.reason: Latin "flagellum" is a whip or scourge; "a flog" is not an English noun.

corrections.old: Hereupon therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he did not only break the sabbath but also said God was his Father, making himself equal to God.
corrections.new: Hereupon therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he did not only break the sabbath but also said God was his Father, making himself equal to God. Then Jesus answered, and said to them:
corrections.reason: English omitted the closing clause 'Respondit itaque Jesus, et dixit eis', which the Clementine Latin places in this verse.

corrections.old: Then Jesus answered them: Amen, amen, I say to you, the Son cannot do anything of himself, but what he sees the Father doing: for what things soever he does, these the Son also does in like manner.
corrections.new: Amen, amen, I say to you, the Son cannot do anything of himself, but what he sees the Father doing: for what things soever he does, these the Son also does in like manner.
corrections.reason: English began with 'Then Jesus answered them', which the Clementine Latin has at the end of 5:18, not in this verse.

corrections.old: Now the pasch, the festival day of the Jews, was near near.
corrections.new: Now the pasch, the festival day of the Jews, was near.
corrections.reason: English duplicated 'near' ('was near near'); the Latin 'proximum' has it once.

corrections.old: Now the Jews feast of tabernacles was near.
corrections.new: Now the Jews' feast of tabernacles was near.
corrections.reason: Typography: missing apostrophe.

corrections.old: And his brothers said to, him: Pass from here and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do.
corrections.new: And his brothers said to him: Pass from here and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do.
corrections.reason: Typography: stray comma.

corrections.old: Go up to this festival day: but I go not up to this festival day, because my time is not accomplished.
corrections.new: Go up to this festival day: but I go not up to this festival day, because my time is not yet accomplished.
corrections.reason: Latin "nondum impletum est" means 'not yet accomplished'; the English omitted 'yet'.

corrections.old: Again therefore, Jesus spoke to: them, saying: I am the light of the world. He that follows me walks not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
corrections.new: Again therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying: I am the light of the world. He that follows me walks not in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
corrections.reason: Typography: stray colon.

corrections.old: The Jews therefore said: Will he kill himself, because he said: Whither I go cannot come?
corrections.new: The Jews therefore said: Will he kill himself, because he said: Whither I go, you cannot come?
corrections.reason: The English omitted 'you' from "vos non potestis venire" ('you cannot come').

corrections.old: Which of you shall convince me of sin? If I say the truth to you, why do you not believe me:
corrections.new: Which of you shall convince me of sin? If I say the truth to you, why do you not believe me?
corrections.reason: Typography: the Latin is a question ("quare non creditis mihi?").

corrections.old: He said therefore to them: If he be a sinner, I know not. One thing I know, that whereas I was blind. now I see.
corrections.new: He said therefore to them: If he be a sinner, I know not. One thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see.
corrections.reason: Typography: full stop inside the sentence ("cum essem, modo video").

corrections.old: Now we know that God does not hear sinners: but if a man be a server of God and does his, will, him he hears.
corrections.new: Now we know that God does not hear sinners: but if a man be a server of God and does his will, him he hears.
corrections.reason: Typography: stray comma.

corrections.old: All others, as many as have come, are thieves and robbers: and the sheep heard them not.
corrections.new: All, as many as have come, are thieves and robbers: and the sheep heard them not.
corrections.reason: Latin "Omnes quotquot venerunt" means 'All, as many as have come'; the English added 'others', which the Latin lacks.

corrections.old: The disciples say to him: Rabbi, the Jews but now sought to stone you. And go there again?
corrections.new: The disciples say to him: Rabbi, the Jews but now sought to stone you. And do you go there again?
corrections.reason: Latin "iterum vadis illuc" is second person, 'do you go there again'; the English dropped the subject 'you'.

corrections.old: When Mary therefore had come where Jesus was, seeing him, she fell down at his feet and says to him. Lord, if you had been here, my brother had not died.
corrections.new: When Mary therefore had come where Jesus was, seeing him, she fell down at his feet and says to him: Lord, if you had been here, my brother had not died.
corrections.reason: Typography: full stop before the direct speech ("dicit ei: Domine").

corrections.old: Do not fear, daughter of Zion: behold your king comes, sitting on an donkey’s colt.
corrections.new: Do not fear, daughter of Zion: behold your king comes, sitting on a donkey’s colt.
corrections.reason: Typography: "an donkey".

corrections.old: And when supper was done (the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, to betray him),
corrections.new: And when supper was done (the devil having now put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray him),
corrections.reason: Latin 'Judas Simonis Iscariotæ' makes Iscariot the genitive of Simon (son of Simon Iscariot), not an epithet of Judas.

corrections.old: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You shall seek me. And as I said to the Jews: Whither I go cannot come; so I say to you now.
corrections.new: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You shall seek me. And as I said to the Jews: Whither I go you cannot come; so I say to you now.
corrections.reason: The English omitted 'you' (Latin 'vos non potestis venire').

corrections.old: Simon Peter says to him: Lord, where go? Jesus answered: Whither I go, you can not follow me now: but you shall follow hereafter.
corrections.new: Simon Peter says to him: Lord, where do you go? Jesus answered: Whither I go, you can not follow me now: but you shall follow hereafter.
corrections.reason: The English omitted the subject of 'quo vadis' (where do you go).

corrections.old: And where I go know: and the way you know.
corrections.new: And where I go you know: and the way you know.
corrections.reason: The English omitted 'you' (Latin 'scitis', you know).

corrections.old: Otherwise believe for the very works’ sake. Amen, amen, I say to you, he that believes in me, the works that I do, he also shall do: and greater than these shall he do.
corrections.new: Otherwise believe for the very works’ sake. Amen, amen, I say to you, he that believes in me, the works that I do, he also shall do: and greater than these shall he do: because I go to the Father.
corrections.reason: The English omitted the Latin's closing clause 'quia ego ad Patrem vado', which it had placed in 14:13.

corrections.old: Because I go to the Father: and whatever you shall ask the Father in my name, that will I do: that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
corrections.new: And whatever you shall ask the Father in my name, that will I do: that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
corrections.reason: The English began with 'Because I go to the Father', which belongs to Latin 14:12; this verse does not have it.

corrections.old: I will not now speak many things with you. For the prince of this world: comes: and in me he has not anything.
corrections.new: I will not now speak many things with you. For the prince of this world comes: and in me he has not anything.
corrections.reason: Typography: stray colon.

corrections.old: But these things I have told you, that when the hour shall come, you may remember that I told you of them.
corrections.new: But these things I have told you, that when their hour shall come, you may remember that I told you.
corrections.reason: Latin 'hora eorum' is 'their hour'; the English dropped 'their' and added 'of them', which this Latin does not have.

corrections.old: But I told you not these things from the beginning, because I was with you. And now I go to him that sent me, and none of you asks me: Whither go?
corrections.new: But I told you not these things from the beginning, because I was with you. And now I go to him that sent me, and none of you asks me: Whither do you go?
corrections.reason: The English omitted the subject of 'Quo vadis' (whither do you go).

corrections.old: All things whatever the Father has are mine. Therefore I said that he shall receive of me and show it to you.
corrections.new: All things whatever the Father has are mine. Therefore I said that he shall receive of mine and show it to you.
corrections.reason: Latin 'de meo accipiet' is 'receive of mine' (what is mine), not 'of me'.

corrections.old: There, therefore, because of the parasceve of the Jews, they laid Jesus: because the tomb was near near.
corrections.new: There, therefore, because of the parasceve of the Jews, they laid Jesus: because the tomb was near.
corrections.reason: Duplicated word "near near"; Latin "quia juxta erat monumentum" has one "near".

corrections.old: Thomas answered him: My Lord and my God.
corrections.new: Thomas answered and said to him: My Lord and my God.
corrections.reason: Latin "Respondit Thomas, et dixit ei" has both verbs; "and said" was missing.
